name: Troccas
description: Troccas is a traditional Swiss Tarot game played in the Romansh-speaking Surselva region of Grisons. It uses a 78-card Swiss 1JJ Tarot deck with Italian suits. Notable for the 'King and Jack Rule' (King demands Jack surrender) and coded signals (Tschintschar). Partnership play for 4.

content.text: Troccas is a traditional Swiss Tarot game played in the Romansh-speaking Surselva region of Grisons. It uses a 78-card Swiss 1JJ Tarot deck with Italian suits. Notable for the 'King and Jack Rule' (King demands Jack surrender) and coded signals (Tschintschar). Partnership play for 4.

Although the exact history is uncertain, Troccas is thought to have been imported from Italy to Switzerland in the seventeenth century. It took root in the Romansh-speaking Canton Grisons, especially the Surselva region from the Medel and Tujetsch valleys to Ilanz, and has been preserved there as a living tradition. In recent decades it has gained in popularity, with local clubs and tournaments; scholarly accounts include Carla Deplazes' work on Graubünden tarot and tournament rules from Savognin.
78 cards: 4 suits x 14 + 21 trumps + Fool. Points: K/Bagat/TrXXI/Fool=5, Q=4, Cav=3, J=2, others=1. Count in groups of 4, subtract 3. Total 72.
19 each (dealer gets 21, discards 2). Last card face up.
